title: Prove odd-axis Clifford tensor Gram lower bound above one half
body:
## Summary

For every odd axis count n>=3 and every tensor width f>=4n+4, improve the sufficient lower constant for the full projective Gaussian-dyadic Clifford tensor Gram matrix:

```diff
- Gram_f >= (1491359/4161536) I
+ Gram_f >= (14601049/29130752) I > (1/2) I
```

The improvement is exactly 1/7 in this domain. Claim type: scoped written mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. The exact spectrum and optimal constant remain open; no new kappa or physical supplier is claimed.

The new step uses seven commuting Pauli quarter turns whose product is I. Their regular-action adjacency sum is at least -10 I. Averaging over Clifford conjugation gives a 5/7 bound on the rank-one contribution, and the cited higher-rank envelope supplies the remainder. Entrywise Gram multiplication propagates the result beyond the initial width. The even-axis initial width has the opposite rank-one sign and remains outside this improvement.

This answers the odd-axis part of Open next question 2 in Javier Vera's #5714. Credit Hiroki KUMAZAKI #5694 for the displacement-rank count and rational tail certificate, and Ali Romman #5526 for the projective trace/Gram framework. Their classical and native/kernel attribution remains with the pinned sources. The predecessor results are cited, without running their executables or repeating their censuses.

Canonical base: de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a, priority revision 8. The six new files are confined to `research/clifford-seven-rotation-gap/`. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19214984).

## Evidence

- Before: the absolute-row certificate gives lower constant 1491359/4161536, approximately 0.358367. #5714 proves its asymptotic limitation and leaves spectral strengthening open.
- After: the written proof gives 14601049/29130752, approximately 0.501224582187. The verifier prints `PASS_CLIFFORD_SEVEN_ROTATION_GAP`.
- New finite evidence enumerates 135 isotropic three-spaces with uniform point incidence, 1,080 literal endpoint columns, all 4,096 admissible fourth-root tuples, and 512 diagonal-subgroup characters. Forty-nine word mutations, two semantic controls, five scope controls and 120 width fixtures pass.
- Warning-strict normal/optimized registered runs agree exactly. Each was timed locally, approximately 0.065/0.087 seconds under its 120-second limit. Environment: CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, standard library only.
- Package metadata, committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export integrity and both read-only Git-free export replays pass. All ten exported files, including the export manifest, retain their bytes and modes.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/clifford-seven-rotation-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/clifford-seven-rotation-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-seven-rotation-gap
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/clifford-seven-rotation-gap --check-source-history
```

Another CPython 3.12 path can replace the absolute interpreter path. The verifier emits a generated SHA-256-bound receipt to stdout and writes no files. `SOURCES.json` pins the three cited proof/question inputs on the base commit.

The written argument supplies the universal quantifiers; the finite checks corroborate its new local ingredients. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No full three-axis Clifford census, selected cold replay, complete caller, paid/native invoice, ownership/restoration, compiler, precision/tape, stock or outer admission was run or discharged.

## Limitations and unrun proof obligations

- The improvement requires odd n>=3 and f>=4n+4. The even-axis initial-width problem, the exact full-group spectrum and the optimal lower constant remain open.
- The alphabet is the full projective Gaussian-dyadic Clifford group with exact arithmetic. Scalar-phase copies must be combined before using a projective Gram matrix. Arbitrary non-Clifford operators, nonunitary scales, nonlinear leaves and rounded equalities are outside scope.
- The universal statement is a written proof using the cited count and trace inputs. Its finite checks corroborate the new local ingredients. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed; no full three-axis Clifford census or proof-kernel check was run.
- No complete physical caller, paid/native invoice, ownership/restoration proof, finite compiler, precision/tape, stock or outer admission is supplied. The selected cold replay and the five inherited framework assumptions were not discharged. No new kappa or complete multiplication theorem is claimed.

## Related open work

- #5837 proves scalar-chart lifting for selected #5599 instructions at every column multiplicity. This result supplies a quantitative full-Clifford Gram bound and makes no selected-caller admission claim.
- #5779 studies all-Clifford helper-detour tariffs and actual source budgets. Its quantity is a path invoice; this contribution bounds an operator Gram spectrum.
- #5843 studies monomial two-FULL routing with restored identity scratch. Its algebraic endpoint obstruction has a different target from this spectral lower bound.

- #5884 extends #5779 to consecutive queries sharing a detour and evaluates a path invoice on Clifford charts. It does not compute this full-alphabet Gram lower constant.
- #5877 proves an additive tariff for two anticommuting involution query types over a faithful coefficient algebra. Its call-count target differs from this full-projective-group spectral bound.
- #5881 constructs a many-channel immutable-payload response under a monotone tariff. It addresses a temporal delivery quotient and supplies no competing Clifford Gram constant.

The completion refresh read this account's nine other open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-27T10:39:47Z: #5876, #5877, #5878, #5879, #5880, #5881, #5882, #5884 and #5885. None supplies this same odd-axis constant or a conflicting same-instance number. No extra computations were run to check another contribution.

## Open next questions

1. Improve the even-axis bound at f=4n+4 with an upper adjacency or joint-rank argument that handles the negative rank-one coefficient and trivial character.
2. Determine the best odd-axis constant by relating higher displacement classes to the same local subgroups. Local sharpness of the seven-root inequality does not establish full-group spectral sharpness.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: package. This adds an isolated proof and explicit replay hook. The selected frontier and predecessor files are unchanged.
